subject: maths
title: Year 6 Comparing and Ordering Fractions
seo_title: Year 6 Comparing and Ordering Fractions Worksheets: Common Denominators, Number Lines and Percentages (Free, with Answer Key)
standard_text: Apply knowledge of equivalence to compare, order and represent common fractions including halves, thirds and quarters on the same number line and justify their order
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on comparing and ordering fractions for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M6N03): equivalent fractions, simplest form, common denominators, mixed numerals, halves, thirds and quarters on the same number line, and fractions as decimals and percentages. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: To compare fractions, write them with a common denominator, then compare the numerators.
key_sub: 2/3 = 8/12 and 3/4 = 9/12, so 2/3 < 3/4. On a number line cut into twelfths, halves, thirds and quarters all sit on a mark.
body_html:
Equivalent fractions

Equivalent fractions show the same amount. Multiply or divide the numerator and the denominator by the same number. For example, 23 = 812 (× 4). A fraction is in simplest form when the numerator and the denominator have no common factor except 1: 1624 = 23 (÷ 8).

Compare with a common denominator

Find a number that both denominators go into. Write both fractions with that denominator. Then compare the numerators.

Example

Which is greater: 23 or 34?

3 and 4 both go into 12. 23 = 812 and 34 = 912. 9 twelfths > 8 twelfths.

Answer: 34

Order fractions, mixed numerals and improper fractions

Write every number with the same denominator. Change mixed numerals into improper fractions first. Then put the numerators in order.

Example

Order 54, 1 13 and 76 from smallest to largest.

Use twelfths: 54 = 1512, 1 13 = 1612, 76 = 1412.

Answer: 76, 54, 1 13

Halves, thirds and quarters on the same number line

Cut the line from 0 to 1 into twelfths, because 2, 3 and 4 all go into 12. Then every half, third and quarter sits on a mark. Numbers further to the right are greater.

Fractions, decimals and percentages

To compare a fraction with a decimal or a percentage, write them all the same way.

FractionDecimalPercentage
120.550%
140.2525%
340.7575%
150.220%
1100.110%
180.12512.5%
13about 0.33about 33%

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction: 18 > 14A bigger denominator means smaller parts: 18 < 14
Comparing only the numerators: 49 > 12 because 4 > 1Use a common denominator: 49 = 818 and 12 = 918, so 49 < 12
Adding the same number to the top and the bottom: 23 = 45Multiply both by the same number: 23 = 46
Writing the digits side by side: 34 = 34%34 = 75100 = 75%

faq.q: What do Year 6 students learn about comparing and ordering fractions?
faq.a: In the Australian Curriculum (AC9M6N03), Year 6 students use equivalent fractions to compare and order common fractions, place halves, thirds and quarters on the same number line, and explain why the order is correct.

faq.q: How do you compare fractions with different denominators?
faq.a: Write both fractions with a common denominator, then compare the numerators. For 2/3 and 3/4, use twelfths: 2/3 = 8/12 and 3/4 = 9/12, so 3/4 is greater.

faq.q: How do you put halves, thirds and quarters on the same number line?
faq.a: Split the line from 0 to 1 into twelfths, because 2, 3 and 4 all go into 12. Then 1/4 = 3/12, 1/3 = 4/12, 1/2 = 6/12, 2/3 = 8/12 and 3/4 = 9/12.
No. NAPLAN is for Years 3, 5, 7 and 9. Comparing fractions, decimals and percentages in Year 6 helps students get ready for high school and the Year 7 numeracy test.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
13 = ?6
items.e: The bottom bar has 6 equal parts, so each third of the top bar is split into 2 parts. 1 third becomes 1 × 2 = 2 sixths. So 13 = 26.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
34 = ?12
items.e: The bottom bar has 12 equal parts, so each quarter of the top bar is split into 3 parts. 3 quarters become 3 × 3 = 9 twelfths. So 34 = 912.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
25 = ?10
items.e: The bottom bar has 10 equal parts, so each fifth of the top bar is split into 2 parts. 2 fifths become 2 × 2 = 4 tenths. So 25 = 410.

items.q: 23 = ?12
items.e: Look at the denominators: 3 × 4 = 12. Multiply the numerator by 4 too: 2 × 4 = 8. So 23 = 812.

items.q: 56 = ?18
items.e: Look at the denominators: 6 × 3 = 18. Multiply the numerator by 3 too: 5 × 3 = 15. So 56 = 1518.

items.q: 38 = ?24
items.e: Look at the denominators: 8 × 3 = 24. Multiply the numerator by 3 too: 3 × 3 = 9. So 38 = 924.

items.q: 45 = ?20
items.e: Look at the denominators: 5 × 4 = 20. Multiply the numerator by 4 too: 4 × 4 = 16. So 45 = 1620.

items.q: 34 = 15?
items.e: Look at the numerators: 3 × 5 = 15. Multiply the denominator by 5 too: 4 × 5 = 20. So 34 = 1520.

items.q: 23 = 10?
items.e: Look at the numerators: 2 × 5 = 10. Multiply the denominator by 5 too: 3 × 5 = 15. So 23 = 1015.

items.q: 68 of the bar is shaded. The thick lines split it into groups of 2. Write 68 in its simplest form.
items.e: There are 4 groups and 3 of them are shaded, so 68 = 34. This is the same as dividing 6 and 8 by 2.

items.q: 812 of the bar is shaded. The thick lines split it into groups of 4. Write 812 in its simplest form.
items.e: There are 3 groups and 2 of them are shaded, so 812 = 23. This is the same as dividing 8 and 12 by 4.

items.q: Write 1012 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 10 and 12 is 2. Divide both numbers by 2: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 and 12 ÷ 2 = 6. So 1012 = 56.

items.q: Write 1215 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 12 and 15 is 3. Divide both numbers by 3: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 and 15 ÷ 3 = 5. So 1215 = 45.

items.q: Write 1416 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 14 and 16 is 2. Divide both numbers by 2: 14 ÷ 2 = 7 and 16 ÷ 2 = 8. So 1416 = 78.

items.q: Write 1624 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 16 and 24 is 8. Divide both numbers by 8: 16 ÷ 8 = 2 and 24 ÷ 8 = 3. So 1624 = 23. If you divide by a smaller common factor first, keep going until you can’t divide any more.

items.q: Write 1830 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 18 and 30 is 6. Divide both numbers by 6: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 and 30 ÷ 6 = 5. So 1830 = 35. If you divide by a smaller common factor first, keep going until you can’t divide any more.

items.q: Write 2128 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 21 and 28 is 7. Divide both numbers by 7: 21 ÷ 7 = 3 and 28 ÷ 7 = 4. So 2128 = 34.

items.q: Which fraction is not equivalent to 23?
items.e: 45 is not equal to 23: 2 was added to the numerator and the denominator. Adding changes the value. The others are equivalent, because both numbers were multiplied by the same number (× 2, × 4, × 5).

items.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 34?
items.e: 4 × 3 = 12, so multiply the numerator by 3 too: 3 × 3 = 9. So 34 = 912. 64 only multiplies the numerator, 312 only changes the denominator, and 56 adds 2 to both numbers.

items.q: Which fraction is in its simplest form?
items.e: 7 and 12 have no common factor except 1, so 712 is in its simplest form. The others can be simplified: 814 = 47 (÷ 2); 1015 = 23 (÷ 5); 39 = 13 (÷ 3).

items.q: Which is greater: 47 or 67?
items.e: The denominators are the same, so compare the numerators: 6 > 4. So 67 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 35 or 38?
items.e: The numerators are the same. Fifths are bigger parts than eighths, because the whole is cut into fewer parts. So 35 is greater. A bigger denominator does not make a bigger fraction.

items.q: Which is greater: 45 or 47?
items.e: The numerators are the same. Fifths are bigger parts than sevenths, because the whole is cut into fewer parts. So 45 is greater. A bigger denominator does not make a bigger fraction.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which is greater: 23 or 34?
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 23 = 812 and 34 = 912. 9 > 8, so 34 is greater.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which is greater: 35 or 12?
items.e: Use the common denominator 10: 35 = 610 and 12 = 510. 6 > 5, so 35 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 512 or 13?
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 512 and 13 = 412. 5 > 4, so 512 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 35 or 23?
items.e: Use the common denominator 15: 35 = 915 and 23 = 1015. 10 > 9, so 23 is greater. Comparing only the numerators (3 and 2) gives the wrong answer.

items.q: Which is greater: 56 or 78?
items.e: Use the common denominator 24: 56 = 2024 and 78 = 2124. 21 > 20, so 78 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 34 or 45?
items.e: Use the common denominator 20: 34 = 1520 and 45 = 1620. 16 > 15, so 45 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 25 or 38?
items.e: Use the common denominator 40: 25 = 1640 and 38 = 1540. 16 > 15, so 25 is greater. Comparing only the numerators (2 and 3) gives the wrong answer.

items.q: Which is greater: 712 or 58?
items.e: Use the common denominator 24: 712 = 1424 and 58 = 1524. 15 > 14, so 58 is greater. Comparing only the numerators (7 and 5) gives the wrong answer.

items.q: Which is greater: 69 or 46?
items.e: Use the common denominator 18: 69 = 1218 and 46 = 1218. The numerators are the same, so they are equal.

items.q: Which is smaller: 56 or 910?
items.e: Use the common denominator 30: 56 = 2530 and 910 = 2730. 27 > 25, so 910 is greater. So the smaller one is 56.

items.q:
Which sign goes in the box?
56 □ 45
items.e: Use the common denominator 30: 56 = 2530 and 45 = 2430. So 56 > 45. The open side of the sign faces the greater fraction.

items.q:
Which sign goes in the box?
34 □ 912
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 34 = 912. So 34 = 912.

items.q:
Which sign goes in the box?
38 □ 25
items.e: Use the common denominator 40: 38 = 1540 and 25 = 1640. So 38 < 25. The open side of the sign faces the greater fraction.

items.q: Which statement is true?
c: 25 > 12
23 > 35
34 < 58
56 < 45
items.e: Use a common denominator for each pair. 23 = 1015 and 35 = 915, so 23 > 35 is true. The others are false: 34 = 68 > 58; 56 = 2530 > 45 = 2430; 25 = 410 < 12 = 510.

items.q: Which fraction is greater than 12?
items.e: Half of the denominator is the numerator of one half. Half of 7 is 3.5, and 4 > 3.5, so 47 is greater than 12. Half of 8 is 4 (3 < 4), half of 5 is 2.5 (2 < 2.5) and half of 12 is 6 (5 < 6), so the others are less than 12.

items.q: Which is greater: 1 23 or 74?
items.e: 74 = 1 34. Both have 1 whole, so compare 23 and 34. Use twelfths: 23 = 812 and 34 = 912. 9 > 8, so 74 is greater.

items.q: Jack says, “49 is greater than 12, because 4 is greater than 1.” Is he right?
c: No. 49 is less than 12
items.e: Comparing only the numerators does not work. Use eighteenths: 49 = 818 and 12 = 918. 8 < 9, so 49 is less than 12.

sets.title: Order fractions, mixed numerals and improper fractions

items.q: Which fraction is the greatest?
items.e: All the numerators are 3, so look at the size of the parts. Quarters are the biggest parts here, so 34 is the greatest. 310 has the biggest denominator, so it is the smallest.

items.q: Which fraction is the greatest?
items.e: Use the common denominator 24: 23 = 1624, 34 = 1824, 58 = 1524, 712 = 1424. The greatest is 1824, so the answer is 34.

items.q: Which fraction is the smallest?
items.e: Use the common denominator 30: 23 = 2030, 35 = 1830, 710 = 2130, 56 = 2530. The smallest is 1830, so the answer is 35.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Use the common denominator 24: 74 = 4224, 1 23 = 4024, 1 56 = 4424, 138 = 3924. The greatest is 4424, so the answer is 1 56.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 2 14 = 2712, 73 = 2812, 2 16 = 2612, 52 = 3012. The smallest is 2612, so the answer is 2 16.

Order from smallest to largest:
34, 23, 12
c: 34, 12, 23
34, 23, 12
12, 23, 34
23, 34, 12
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 34 = 912, 23 = 812, 12 = 612. So the order is 12, 23, 34.

25, 13, 12
c: 25, 13, 12
13, 25, 12
13, 12, 25

items.e: Use the common denominator 30: 25 = 1230, 13 = 1030, 12 = 1530. So the order is 13, 25, 12.

56, 34, 78
c: 78, 56, 34
34, 56, 78

38, 14, 13
c: 13, 14, 38
38, 13, 14
14, 13, 38

items.q:
Order from largest to smallest:
45, 710, 34
c: 45, 34, 710
34, 45, 710
710, 45, 34
710, 34, 45
items.e: Use the common denominator 20: 45 = 1620, 710 = 1420, 34 = 1520. So the order is 45, 34, 710.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:
54, 1 13, 76
c: 54, 1 13, 76
76, 54, 1 13
1 13, 54, 76
54, 76, 1 13
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 54 = 1512, 1 13 = 1612, 76 = 1412. So the order is 76, 54, 1 13.

items.q:
Order from largest to smallest:
53, 1 58, 1 34
c: 53, 1 34, 1 58
1 58, 53, 1 34
1 58, 1 34, 53
1 34, 53, 1 58
items.e: Use the common denominator 24: 53 = 4024, 1 58 = 3924, 1 34 = 4224. So the order is 1 34, 53, 1 58.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:
2 12, 73, 94
c: 94, 73, 2 12
2 12, 73, 94
2 12, 94, 73
73, 2 12, 94
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 2 12 = 3012, 73 = 2812, 94 = 2712. So the order is 94, 73, 2 12.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:
23, 12, 34, 13
c: 34, 23, 13, 12
12, 23, 13, 34
12, 13, 23, 34
13, 12, 23, 34
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 23 = 812, 12 = 612, 34 = 912, 13 = 412. So the order is 13, 12, 23, 34.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:
56, 23, 34, 712
c: 56, 34, 23, 712
712, 23, 34, 56
712, 56, 34, 23
23, 34, 56, 712
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 56 = 1012, 23 = 812, 34 = 912, 712. So the order is 712, 23, 34, 56.

items.q:
Order from largest to smallest:
1 14, 32, 43, 1 16
c: 1 14, 32, 43, 1 16
1 14, 32, 1 16, 43
32, 43, 1 14, 1 16
1 16, 1 14, 43, 32
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 1 14 = 1512, 32 = 1812, 43 = 1612, 1 16 = 1412. So the order is 32, 43, 1 14, 1 16.

items.q: Which fraction is between 13 and 12?
items.e: Use twelfths: 13 = 412 and 12 = 612. 512 is between them. 14 = 312 is too small, and 23 = 812 and 712 are too big.

items.q: Which number is between 1 12 and 1 34?
items.e: Use eighths: 1 12 = 128 and 1 34 = 148. 138 = 1 58 is between them. 118 and 54 are too small, and 158 is too big.

items.q: Which fraction is closest to 1?
items.e: Look at the part that is missing from 1 whole: 78 needs 18, 45 needs 15, 56 needs 16 and 910 needs 110. 110 is the smallest missing part, so 910 is closest to 1.

items.q: Which fraction is the smallest?
items.e: Each fraction is 1 part short of 1 whole: 15, 16, 17 and 18 are missing. 15 is the biggest missing part, so 45 is the smallest.

sets.title: Halves, thirds and quarters on the same number line

items.q: Which letter shows 53?
items.e: Each whole is split into 6 equal parts, so each mark is 16. 53 = 1 23. 23 = 46. Go to 1, then 4 more marks. That is letter D.

items.q: Which letter shows 23?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 is split into twelfths. 23 = 812 (multiply both numbers by 4), so count 8 marks from 0. That is letter B. Don’t count only 2 marks: each mark is 112, not 13.

items.q: Which letter shows 34?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 is split into twelfths. 34 = 912 (multiply both numbers by 3), so count 9 marks from 0. That is letter C. Don’t count only 3 marks: each mark is 112, not 14.

items.q: Which letter shows 13?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 is split into twelfths. 13 = 412 (multiply both numbers by 4), so count 4 marks from 0. That is letter A. Don’t count only 1 mark: each mark is 112, not 13.

items.q: Which letter shows 56?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 is split into twelfths. 56 = 1012 (multiply both numbers by 2), so count 10 marks from 0. That is letter C. Don’t count only 5 marks: each mark is 112, not 16.

items.q: Which letter shows 1 13?
items.e: Each whole is split into 6 equal parts, so each mark is 16. 13 = 26. Go to 1, then 2 more marks. That is letter A.

items.q: Which letter shows 54?
items.e: Each whole is split into 8 equal parts, so each mark is 18. 54 = 1 14. 14 = 28. Go to 1, then 2 more marks. That is letter D.

items.q: Which letter shows 94?
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. 94 = 2 14. Go to 2, then 1 more mark. That is letter B.

items.q: Which letter shows 1 34?
items.e: Each whole is split into 8 equal parts, so each mark is 18. 34 = 68. Go to 1, then 6 more marks. That is letter C.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give the fraction in simplest form.
items.e: Each whole is split into 6 equal parts, so each mark is 16. The arrow is 4 marks after 0, so it shows 46. Simplify: 46 = 23 (÷ 2). The answer is 23. Count the spaces between marks, not the marks themselves.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give the fraction in simplest form.
items.e: Each whole is split into 12 equal parts, so each mark is 112. The arrow is 9 marks after 0, so it shows 912. Simplify: 912 = 34 (÷ 3). The answer is 34. Count the spaces between marks, not the marks themselves.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give the mixed numeral in simplest form.
items.e: Each whole is split into 6 equal parts, so each mark is 16. The arrow is 3 marks after 1, so it shows 1 36. Simplify: 36 = 12 (÷ 3). The answer is 1 12. Count the spaces between marks, not the marks themselves.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give the mixed numeral in simplest form.
items.e: Each whole is split into 8 equal parts, so each mark is 18. The arrow is 6 marks after 1, so it shows 1 68. Simplify: 68 = 34 (÷ 2). The answer is 1 34. Count the spaces between marks, not the marks themselves.

items.q: The two number lines are the same length. Which is greater: 23 or 34?
items.e: The dot further to the right shows the greater number. Check with the common denominator 12: 23 = 812 and 34 = 912. So 34 is greater.

items.q: The two number lines are the same length. Which is greater: 56 or 34?
items.e: The dot further to the right shows the greater number. Check with the common denominator 12: 56 = 1012 and 34 = 912. So 56 is greater.

items.q: The two number lines are the same length. Which is greater: 43 or 54?
items.e: The dot further to the right shows the greater number. Check with the common denominator 12: 43 = 1612 and 54 = 1512. So 43 is greater.

items.q: Which fraction is exactly halfway between 12 and 1 on a number line?
items.e: Use quarters: 12 = 24 and 1 = 44. Halfway between 2 quarters and 4 quarters is 34. 23 is between them too, but it is not halfway.

items.q: Which fraction is exactly halfway between 14 and 12 on a number line?
items.e: Use eighths: 14 = 28 and 12 = 48. Halfway between 2 eighths and 4 eighths is 38. 13 = 824 is between them, but it is not halfway.

items.q: Which number is exactly halfway between 1 and 1 12 on a number line?
items.e: Use quarters: 1 12 = 1 24. Halfway between 1 and 1 24 is 1 14. 1 13 is between them, but it is not halfway.

items.q: Mia marks 12, 13 and 14 on the same number line from 0 to 1. Which one is closest to 0?
c: They are all the same distance
items.e: Use twelfths: 12 = 612, 13 = 412 and 14 = 312. The smallest is 312, so 14 is closest to 0. Quarters are smaller parts than thirds and halves.

sets.title: Fractions, decimals and percentages in word problems

items.q: Write 34 as a percentage.
items.e: 34 = 75100, because 4 × 25 = 100 and 3 × 25 = 75. So 34 = 75%. 34% just writes the digits 3 and 4 side by side.

items.q: Write 25 as a decimal.
items.e: 25 = 410 (multiply both numbers by 2). 4 tenths = 0.4. 0.25 just writes the digits 2 and 5, and 2.5 is 5 ÷ 2.

items.q: Write 0.6 as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.6 is 6 tenths = 610. Divide both numbers by 2: 35. 6100 is 0.06, not 0.6, and 23 is about 0.67.

items.q: Which percentage is equal to 15?
items.e: 15 = 20100, because 5 × 20 = 100. So 15 = 20%.

items.q: Write 18 as a percentage.
items.e: 18 is half of 14. 14 = 25%, so 18 = 25% ÷ 2 = 12.5%. It is not 8% or 18%.

items.q: Which is not equal to 12?
items.e: 12 = 510 = 0.5 = 50%. 0.05 is 5 hundredths, which is much smaller than one half.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:
0.7, 34, 65%
items.e: Write them all as percentages: 0.7 = 70%, 34 = 75%, 65%. So the order is 65%, 0.7, 34.

items.q: Which is the greatest?
items.e: Write them all as decimals: 0.35, 25 = 0.4, 30% = 0.3, 38 = 0.375. The greatest is 0.4, so 25.

items.q: In a maths quiz, Mia scores 45 of the marks, Leo scores 78% and Zara scores 0.75. Who does best?
items.e: Write them all as percentages: 45 = 80%, 78% and 0.75 = 75%. So Mia does best.

items.q: The forecast gives a 30% chance of rain on Saturday and a 14 chance on Sunday. Which day is more likely to be wet?
items.e: 14 = 25%, and 30% is more than 25%. So rain is more likely on Saturday.

items.q: Kai’s tablet battery shows 45%. Sienna’s tablet battery is 12 full. Whose tablet has more charge?
items.e: 12 = 50%, and 50% is more than 45%. So Sienna’s tablet has more charge.

items.q: At the swimming carnival, 35 of the Year 6 students swim in a race. What percentage is that?
items.e: 35 = 60100 (multiply both numbers by 20). So 60% of the students swim in a race, which is more than half.

items.q: On Monday the canteen sells 0.6 of its sausage rolls. On Tuesday it sells 23 of the same number of sausage rolls. On which day does it sell more?
items.e: Use fifteenths: 0.6 = 35 = 915 and 23 = 1015. 10 > 9, so it sells more on Tuesday. (23 is about 0.67.)

items.q: Grace has a 1 L water bottle with 750 mL of water in it. What fraction of the bottle is full?
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL. 7501000 = 34 (divide both numbers by 250). So the bottle is 34 full. 14 is the empty part.

items.q: Mum fills the car with petrol when the tank is below 40%. The fuel gauge shows 38 of a tank. Should she fill it now?
c: No. 38 is more than 40%
No. 38 is about half a tank
items.e: 38 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375 = 37.5%. 37.5% is below 40%, so yes, she should fill it now.

items.q: A footy team wins 13 of its 20 games. What percentage of its games does it win?
items.e: 1320 = 65100 (multiply both numbers by 5). So the team wins 65% of its games.

items.q: In a fun run, Oliver has run 0.8 km, Isla has run 34 km and Noah has run 710 km. Order them from the furthest to the shortest distance.
items.e: Write them all as decimals: 0.8, 34 = 0.75 and 710 = 0.7. So the order is Oliver, Isla, Noah.

items.q: A pair of shoes costs the same price in two shops. Shop A takes 25% off. Shop B takes 15 off. Which shop gives the bigger discount?
items.e: 15 = 20%, and 25% is more than 20%. So Shop A gives the bigger discount. Don’t compare 25 with 5.

items.q: Ava says 0.3 = 13. Is she right?
c: No. 13 is less than 0.3
No. 13 is more than 0.3
items.e: 0.3 = 310. In thirtieths: 310 = 930 and 13 = 1030. So 13 is more than 0.3. (13 = 0.333…)

items.q: Liam has read 58 of a book. Matilda has read 60% of the same book. Who has read more?
items.e: 58 = 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625 = 62.5%. 62.5% is more than 60%, so Liam has read more.
